about: Tour stops for the interactive Storyraise Collect stories demo. Seven product screens; each stop names the screen and state it describes. Copy uses the product's own labels, checked against the code cited in `source` (Collect = storyraise-collect branch; builder/reader = main). American English, no em dashes.

stops.title: Start a collection
stops.tells: A collection holds one form and every response to it. Start new collection from Collections.
stops.why: Each collection becomes a data source your reports can repeat over.
stops.next: Name it for what you are gathering, like Scholarship Stories.

uiLabel: What do you want to collect?
stops.title: Choose what you want to collect
stops.tells: Pick a starting point: thank-yous from beneficiaries, stories from program leaders, the field, or your community, general information, or an upload.
stops.why: Each one starts the form with sensible questions, so you edit instead of starting from a blank page.
stops.next: Here it is Thank-yous from beneficiaries, for students writing to the donors who fund them.

stops.title: Add the fields you need
stops.tells: Add Fields offers short and long text, email, phone, choices, dropdowns, numbers, dates, and file uploads, plus headings and paragraphs to organize the form.
stops.why: A name, a story, and a photo are all it takes to fill a report with real people.
stops.next: Click a field type to add it, then click the field to edit it.

stops.title: Every field saves to a variable
stops.tells: In the field editor, Save to Variable names the answer. This one saves to student_note, so a report can show it as @@student_note@@.
stops.why: The variable name is the link between the form and your report. Choose short, clear names.
stops.next: Set the label your respondents see, the variable your report uses, and whether the field is required.

stops.title: Photos and videos come in as uploads
stops.tells: A File upload field can accept any file, or only images, videos, or documents. This one takes images only.
stops.why: Respondents send their own photos from a phone or computer, and the photo arrives with their story.
stops.next: Use Videos only for a short video message.

stops.title: Share one link
stops.tells: Get form link gives you the link to send by email, text, or social media. Anyone with it can respond.
stops.why: No accounts or apps for respondents, just a link that works on any device.
stops.next: Copy form link, or View form to see what respondents see.

stops.title: What respondents see
stops.tells: The form carries your logo and questions. Here Sophia Ramirez writes her note and adds her photo.
stops.why: Stories in the respondent's own words read as far more genuine than anything written for them.
stops.next: Submit sends the response straight into the collection.

stops.title: Every response, one row
stops.tells: Responses land in the collection as rows, one per student, with every field in its own column.
stops.why: You can review, edit, import, or export them before any of it appears in a report.
stops.next: Open any response to review or edit it.

stops.title: Add a Repeater
stops.tells: In the builder's Insert panel, drag a Repeater onto the page where the stories should go.
stops.why: A Repeater is a block that copies itself once for every matching row in a collection.
stops.next: Then select it and open Use Data.

stops.title: Point a repeater at the collection
stops.tells: Select a Repeater block, open Use Data, and under Repeat For Each Item in, select your collection.
stops.why: The block repeats once for every response, so the report grows as stories come in.
stops.next: Lay out one card inside it.

source.note: Repeat For Each Item in panel

stops.title: Design one card
stops.tells: Inside the repeater, use the form's variables: @@student_name@@, @@class_year@@, @@major@@, @@student_note@@, and the photo from @@student_photo@@.
stops.why: You design a single card once, and every response fills its own copy.
stops.next: Next, give the card each student's photo.

stops.title: Each student's own photo
stops.tells: Select the card's photo block, open Use Data, and under Override Media choose Use Media from a Variable: @@student_photo@@. In the editor you see a placeholder; each student's photo fills in when the report opens.
stops.why: The photo each student uploaded appears on their own card, with no downloading or resizing.
stops.next: For a video field, select a Video element and use Use Video from a Variable.

uiLabel: Enter the value to look for
stops.title: Make it personal
stops.tells: Under Repeat When, pick the column fund_id, the condition is, and the value @@fund_reference@@, the code on the donor's own record.
stops.why: Each donor sees the students their gift supports, and nobody else's.
stops.next: Sort and Limit can order the cards and cap how many show. A repeater needs a Repeat When to show anything.
keepInMind: is needs an exact match, capitals included, even with Case-insensitive matching checked; that box only applies to contains. A Dropdown list whose options are the codes avoids typos.
Repeaters fill in when a donor opens their personalized link. Without ?for=, the page shows the card's variables as typed.

stops.title: The donor's side of the match
stops.tells: Emily Wilson's record carries @@fund_reference@@, F004, the fund her gift supports. It came in as a column of her donor list, from a CSV import or your CRM.
stops.why: That shared code is what lets a report pick the right students for each donor.
stops.next: Make sure the codes on donor records and the codes students enter look exactly alike.

stops.title: Emily meets her students
stops.tells: Emily Wilson gives to the Health Sciences Innovation Fund, so her report shows Sophia Ramirez, a nursing student, and David Chen, who studies public health.
stops.why: The same report reads as a personal update from the people her gift helped.
stops.next: Switch to James Taylor to compare.

stops.title: James meets his
stops.tells: James Taylor gives to the STEM Research Endowment, so he sees Grace Johnson and Marcus Lee instead.
stops.why: One report, one link, and every donor reads the stories behind their own gift.
stops.next: Send it with the personalized link from Share, or with Storyraise Send.

stops.title: Or link one story to one donor
stops.tells: Instead of matching a shared code, you can tag a response to the donors it belongs to: Make Edits, then Assign to... Constituents. Here Sophia's story is tagged to Emily Wilson.
stops.why: Useful when there is no shared field, like a thank-you meant for one major donor.
stops.next: Then set the repeater to Repeat When constituents contains @@id@@.
keepInMind: Use contains, not is: a response can be tagged to several donors, and is never matches a list.

source.note: is never matches an array; use contains
